title: Related content: Partial-text indexing

judge.reasoning:
Patch B resolves the issue directly and is the better fix. It adds an opt-in `splitWords` flag for string indices such as title. Values are split on characters that are not letters, numbers or marks, which is Unicode-aware. Words are deduplicated per document, so repeated words cannot inflate rank. It also adds configurable `stopWords`, which the issue explicitly suggests for ignoring common words in an i18n-friendly way. The routing goes through the existing StringsToKeywords/ToKeywords paths, so both indexing and querying are consistent. It rejects the unsupported fragments combination at config decode time with a clear error and documents the new options. Its tests are meaningful and would fail before the change: unit tests cover splitting, Unicode, stop words and dedup; search tests cover named slices, document search and stop-word exclusion; there is a config decode test including the fragments error; and an integration test compares results with and without splitWords.

Patch A adds `tokenize` and `minTokenLength` and extends tokenization to fragment heading titles, which adds complexity and risk:
- For fragments, tokenized heading words become `StringKeyword` (via stringToKeyword), not `FragmentKeyword`. The ApplyFilter branch only collects words when `kw.(FragmentKeyword)` succeeds, so `ff.words` appears never to be populated. The tokenized applyFilter path therefore looks broken, which casts doubt on its own ApplyFilter test.
- The plain string/[]string tokenize path does not deduplicate repeated words within a value, so rank can be inflated. Dedup was added only for fragments.
- It has no stop-word support; minTokenLength is a cruder substitute.
- It mixes in unrelated whitespace churn in an existing test file.
- It has no docs and no config validation.

Overall, B is more correct, better scoped, better tested and better documented.

issue_md:
When specifying the indices for related content, it would be useful to specify that some of them were split by word, so that their text could be matched partially. This would allow the title to be used for more in-depth indexing, rather than requiring the user to specify tags / keywords.

This would likely increase memory usage and decrease performance, so should definitely be opt-in!

I suspect common words (a, an, the etc) might want to be ignored? Although doing that in a sane, i18n-friendly manner might be a challenge!

Setting "2006" (default value for date indexes) as the pattern for a date index will add weight to pages published in the same year. For busier blogs, "200601" (year and month) may be a better default.
 
+`splitWords`
+: (`bool`) Whether to split string values into words before indexing them, so that text such as the page `title` can be matched partially. +`stopWords`
+: (`[]string`) Words to ignore when `splitWords` is enabled, for example `['a', 'an', 'the']`. Matched case-insensitively. Default is none.
+
 `toLower`
 : (`bool`) Whether to transform keywords in both the indexes and the queries to lower case. This may give more accurate results at a slight performance penalty. Default is `false`.

+func splitWords(title string) []string {
+	// Fast path: no whitespace or HTML entities means at most one token.
+	if strings.IndexFunc(title, unicode.IsSpace) == -1 && strings.IndexByte(title, '&') == -1 {
+		title = strings.TrimFunc(html.UnescapeString(title), func(r rune) bool { return !unicode.IsLetter(r) && !unicode.IsDigit(r) })
+		if title == "" {
+			return nil
+		}
+		return []string{title}
+	}
+	raw := strings.Fields(html.UnescapeString(title))
+	words := raw[:0]
+	for _, w := range raw {
+		w = strings.TrimFunc(w, func(r rune) bool { return !unicode.IsLetter(r) && !unicode.IsDigit(r) })
+		if w != "" {

title: The "failed to extract" error refers to outer shortcode instead of inner shortcode

judge.reasoning:
The bug: an unclosed nested shortcode (`img`) swallows content until it reaches the outer `{{< /figure >}}` closing tag. That tag gets treated as `img`'s closing, which leaves `figure` apparently unclosed, so the error names the wrong shortcode.

Patch B fixes this at the root. When the closing tag's name doesn't match the shortcode being extracted, it raises an error naming the inner shortcode ("shortcode \"img\" must be closed or self-closed"). It also gives a specific message for a stray closing tag on a shortcode that doesn't use `.Inner`. Its tests reproduce the exact scenario from the issue (figure/img/figcaption) and assert the error names `img` and not `figure`. They also cover the top-level unclosed case, the stray closing tag case, and a positive case with valid nesting. These tests would fail before the change and pass after.

Patch A only re-wraps errors from nested extraction with the nested shortcode's position. It does not change how a mismatched closing tag is matched, so the issue's scenario would still report `unclosed shortcode \"figure\"`. Its test covers a different situation (inner template not found) and never exercises the unclosed-nested case from the issue. Patch A therefore does not resolve the reported problem.

Patch B is correct and well tested; Patch A misses the root cause.

title: resources/images: Poor overlay quality when background image is an indexed (not true color) PNG

judge.reasoning:
Both patches make the same core fix. They introduce `images.ActionFilter`, use it in `Filter`, and skip the step that re-applies the source palette when `conf.Action == ActionFilter`. Filtered output from an indexed PNG is therefore no longer clamped to the 256-color source palette, which is the root cause in the issue. Both also update the paletted overlay and text golden images identically.

The difference is everything else.

Patch A bundles a separate change to color handling that the issue does not ask for:
- Hex strings now parse to `color.NRGBA` instead of `color.RGBA`.
- `Color.init` normalizes colors to NRGBA.
- `ColorGoToHexString` now un-premultiplies.
- `AddColorToPalette` now compares color values instead of interface values.

This changes observable behavior: test expectations were rewritten and the `padding-transparent-chained` golden image changed. It belongs to a different issue, adds regression risk to padding, text and color APIs, and obscures the fix. Patch A's new tests cover only that color change, not the overlay-on-indexed-PNG problem; for the actual issue it relies solely on the golden-image updates.

Patch B stays focused and adds a targeted integration test. It runs Overlay, Text and Colorize filters on an indexed PNG and asserts that:
- the output is not paletted;
- it contains colors outside the source palette;
- the overlay output has at least 1000 colors.

It also checks that Resize still keeps the palette. This test would fail before the fix and pass after it. Its comments and the doc comment on `ActionFilter` are clear.

With correctness equal, Patch B wins on tests and on scope.

title: Automatic summary may generate invalid HTML with blockquotes and lists

judge.reasoning:
Both patches fix the core bug the same way: after the word-count cutoff, they push the summary end forward until the open block elements are closed. Both add unit and integration tests for blockquotes and lists that would fail before the change and pass after it. The main difference is correctness across markup formats. **Patch A** tracks every non-void element, including `div` and `section`, for all formats. AsciiDoc output wraps entire sections in `div.sect1`/`div.sectionbody`, and Org output similarly nests whole sections in divs. Patch A would therefore stretch an AsciiDoc or Org summary to the end of the enclosing section, often most of the document. This is a likely regression for non-Markdown content. Patch A also relies on a hand-written HTML tag scanner. It handles comments, quoted attributes and raw-text elements, but it is a large amount of bespoke parsing code that adds maintenance risk. Finally, it rewrites the existing `BenchmarkSummaryFromHTML`, dropping its correctness assertions and replacing `b.Loop()` with `b.N`. That is unrelated churn that weakens existing coverage. **Patch B** uses `golang.org/x/net/html`'s tokenizer, which is robust and already a Hugo dependency. It only tracks a curated set of block containers matching the elements listed in the issue's spec quote, plus raw-text elements. It deliberately treats `div`/`section` as containers only for Markdown and HTML, which avoids the AsciiDoc/RST/Org whole-section problem. Its tests cover several important cases: - nested list and blockquote - a div in Markdown - a blockquote at the end of the document - a `

` inside a script - an RST document wrapper, showing that `WrapperStart`/`WrapperEnd` still work correctly Its integration test also checks `Truncated` and `ContentWithoutSummary`. Patch B's per-call map and tokenizer allocations are a minor performance cost. Overall, Patch B is the more correct and safer fix with better-targeted tests and no damage to existing tests.

### What version of Hugo are you using (`hugo version`)? 
$ hugo version
hugo v0.151.0+extended+withdeploy darwin/arm64 BuildDate=2025-10-02T13:30:36Z VendorInfo=brew
### Does this issue reproduce with the latest release? Yes ## Issue Using a blockquote that extends past the `.Summary` cutoff causes the content below `{{ .Summary }}` to be treated as part of the blockquote until the end of the parent tag. [Reproduction repo](https://github.com/imomaliev/hugo-blockquote-summary-leak) Hugo's `.Summary` may lead to `blockquote` end tag be below cutoff point ## Explanation In most modern browsers this html code will be parsed and rendered without errors ```html

1

``` Leading to shown in browser as a source ```html

1

``` This is due to [these parsing rules](html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#parsing-main-inbody#:~:text=An%20end%20tag%20whose%20tag%20name%20is%20one%20of%3A%20%22address%22%2C%20%22article%22%2C%20%22aside%22%2C%20%22blockquote%22) > An end tag whose tag name is one of: "address", "article", "aside", "blockquote", "button", "center", "details", "dialog", "dir", "div", "dl", "fieldset", "figcaption", "figure", "footer", "header", "hgroup", "listing", "main", "menu", "nav", "ol", "pre", "search", "section", "select", "summary", "ul" > > If the stack of open elements does not have an element in scope that is an HTML element with the same tag name as that of the token, then this is a parse error; ignore the token. > > Otherwise, run these steps: > > Generate implied end tags. > > If the current node is not an HTML element with the same tag name as that of the token, then this is a parse error. > > Pop elements from the stack of open elements until an HTML element with the same tag name as the token has been popped from the stack. ## To Discuss I think the best case scenario is for `.Summary` to handle generation of implied tags. But I am not sure how to do that myself. For now I plan to provide a PR with fixes for a theme and docs, to avoid confusion and errors - https://github.com/gohugoio/hugo/pull/14045 - https://github.com/gohugoio/hugoDocs/pull/3230

title: Support slug in section, taxonomy, and term pages

judge.reasoning: Patch A does not address slug support for section, taxonomy, or term pages. It renames an interface parameter, fixing the typo `HasAnyVectorv`, and switches `MatchSiteVector` from `HasAnyVector` to `HasVector`. Neither change touches URL or slug computation, and A adds no tests. Patch B works on the slug feature directly. It records the slugs of ancestor branch nodes in the walk context and compares them between the previous and current build. When an ancestor slug changes, it rebuilds descendants from source and marks their identities as changed, so target paths of all descendant pages update. This is exactly the issue's requirement that a section slug affect the section and all descendants, and it covers the server/rebuild case. B also clones the term `sitesMatrixBase` map so a later merge cannot mutate it, which keeps rebuild-from-source correct for terms. B adds a thorough rebuild test covering changing, removing and adding nested section slugs and changing a taxonomy slug, plus a taxonomy cascade rebuild test. It changes one existing assertion to expect an absolute RSS link; this is a minor, unexplained change but plausible. B is the only patch that meaningfully addresses the issue, with substantive tests.

issue_md:
<!-- Describe this new feature. Think about if it really belongs in the Hugo core module; you may want to discuss it on https://discourse.gohugo.io/ first.  -->

Currently with multilanguage sites you can localize the URL for pages by setting `slug` in the frontmatter.

However there is no `slug` support for sections. This means the only way to localize a section URL is to use `url` together with `[[cascade]]`. This is annoying since you have to "redo from scratch" the entire URL format, with `:` tokens, duplicating names for parent sections, etc.

Proposal: add support for `slug` in section pages. It would behave the obvious way, basically being equivalent to changing the directory name for the section. It would affect the URL for the section and all descendant pages.

Example:

```
help/
    _index.en.md    # contains no slug
    _index.es.md    # contains slug="ayuda"
    how-to-frob/
       index.en.md    # contains no slug
       index.es.md    # contains slug="como-frobear"
```

would result in the following paths:

```
help/
help/how-to-frob/
es/ayuda/
es/ayuda/como-frobear/
```

title: Make default baseUrl https://example.org/

judge.reasoning:
Both patches make the default baseURL https://example.org/. Patch A puts it in `newDefaultConfig()`, the function that already holds Hugo's other defaults (taxonomies, sitemap, environment). User config, language config and the `--baseURL` flag then override it through the normal merge. Patch B instead overwrites an empty `c.BaseURL` inside `CompileConfig`. That works, but it replaces any empty value, including one the user set explicitly, and it hides a default inside compilation logic instead of the defaults table. It also leaves the raw config value empty for any code that reads it before compilation. Patch A's placement addresses the root cause more cleanly.

Tests: Patch A adds focused integration tests for the default value (checking both `Configs.Base.BaseURL` and the per-site compiled BaseURL), the multilingual non-multihost case, and an explicit override. It also adds a command testscript covering the `--baseURL` flag and a server testscript showing the default is rewritten to localhost in `hugo server`. That is much broader scenario coverage. Patch B adds one simple test for set, unset and "/" cases. Its other test changes mostly pin `baseURL = "/"` to keep old expectations, which tests less of the new behaviour than A's approach of updating expectations to the new absolute URLs.

Scope and craft: Patch B includes a lot of unrelated reformatting (splitting `AssertFileContent(` arguments onto new lines across many tests). This obscures the actual change and accounts for most of its diff. Patch A's diff is limited to the behaviour change and its test consequences.

issue_md:
If I want to create a very basic site, the only reason I currently need to create a config file is to set the `baseUrl`.

So, having the `baseURL` default to https://example.org/  would be a slightly breaking change, but it would solve more issues than it introduces.

title: Add build.cleanDestinationDir config option

judge.reasoning:
Both patches let users keep extra files such as `.git`, `.domains`, `_redirects` and nested paths when `--cleanDestinationDir` runs. B is preferred because it solves the issue additively with less risk.

Patch B adds `build.cleanDestinationDir.keep`, a list of globs matched against the path relative to the publishDir. It leaves the existing behavior intact: the root `cleanDestinationDir` bool and flag still work, and `.gitignore`, `.gitattributes` and dot-directories are still always preserved. The change to the `keep` callback is minimal: it passes the destination-relative path in addition to the FileInfo. A matched directory is kept whole, which covers the issue's file-or-directory examples. B includes:
- a unit test of compiling and matching the globs, including leading-slash input, nested paths, the `**` behavior, invalid-glob errors and cloning;
- a new testscript built around the issue's exact scenario (a worktree `.git` file, `.domains`, `_redirects`, `foo/bar/.mysecretfile`), run with and without a static dir;
- documentation, including the multihost caveat.

Patch A is a broader redesign. It moves the setting to `build.cleanDestinationDir.enable`, deprecates and removes `RootConfig.CleanDestinationDir`, remaps the CLI flag to a nested key, and splits patterns into `keepFiles` and `keepDirs` with negation support. The hard-coded defaults become overridable default patterns. This carries more risk:
- Removing the root field could break any other consumers.
- The flag-to-nested-key mapping and the legacy normalization are new code paths.
- Setting `keepFiles` or `keepDirs` replaces the defaults entirely. A's own scenario 4 shows `.gitignore` and `.hidden/` being deleted once a user adds `.domains`. A user following the issue would therefore silently lose protections they had before, unless they re-list them.

A's default protection of `.git` files is a nice touch, and its testscript coverage is decent. However, the extra surface area and the regression-prone override semantics outweigh those benefits. B fixes the reported need cleanly, stays backward compatible, and has more targeted tests.

<!-- Describe this new feature. Think about if it really belongs in the Hugo core module; you may want to discuss it on https://discourse.gohugo.io/ first.  -->

## Usecase

I'm using Codeberg Pages to host my website, you can find the repostitory at https://codeberg.org/ilovelinux/pages

I have two branches:
- `main`: hugo project
- `pages`: hugo build (output of `public/`)

Since I'm using Codeberg Pages with a custom domain, I also need a `.domains` file[^codebergDomains] to be pushed in the `pages` branch.

### When I

- Have files in the `static/` directory.
- Switch to `main` branch.
- Create the `public/` folder using a git worktree of the `pages` branch.
- Run `hugo build --cleanDestinationDir`.

### I need

- To remove outdated content
- To retain:
  - `.git` **file** created by `git worktree`[^gitWorktreeFile].
  - `.domains` **file** used by Codeberg Pages in order to allow custom domains[^codebergDomains].
  - `_redirects` **file** for redirects (however I'm not using it yet)[^codebergRedirects].

### Instead

- The files I need to be retained are deleted.

## Proposal

Add a configuration field to list relative file paths to `public/` that should be retained when using `--cleanDestinationDir`.

#### Example
```yaml
 filesToRetain:
  - .git
  - .domains
  - _redirects
  - foo/bar/.mysecretfile
```

Files retained:
- `public/.git`
- `public/.domains`
- `public/_redirects`
- `public/foo/bar/.mysecretfile`

> [!NOTE]
> I'm not suggesting to use `filesToRetain` as configuration field, but I couldn't think of a better name.

## Notes

> [!IMPORTANT]
> `--cleanDestinationDir` does nothing when when the `static/` directory doesn't exist since its value is used inside the `copyStaticTo` function.
> https://github.com/gohugoio/hugo/blob/c4bbc2805c7092deafabae01e71ff2dda37bd877/commands/hugobuilder.go#L481

### Workaround

> [!WARNING]
> This approach is error-prone.

I implemented a workaround in my [Makefile](https://codeberg.org/ilovelinux/pages/src/commit/072c6dc048096c98c3422e824cb1d3bbc0b60736/Makefile#L9-L11) that:
- Repairs the worktree folder, as suggested in https://github.com/gohugoio/hugo/pull/6261#issuecomment-1692321365.
- Restores the `.domains` file.

### Related issues & PR
- https://github.com/gohugoio/hugo/issues/3202 was about `.git` **folder** being deleted.
  Fixed thanks to:
  - https://github.com/spf13/fsync/pull/10
  - https://github.com/gohugoio/hugo/pull/3210.
- https://github.com/gohugoio/hugo/issues/4546 was about `.git` **file** of a submodule[^gitSubmoduleFile] being deleted. Closed because it was considered a discussion.
- https://github.com/gohugoio/hugo/pull/6261 was introducing a fix for the `.git` **file** in order to work correctly with git worktrees and submodules. Closed because of the Stale bot but it looks like it was still kept into consideration since @bep kept moving it among milestones after that.
  However this wouldn't solve my issue since `.domains` and `_redirects` files would still be deleted.

[^gitWorktreeFile]: https://git-scm.com/docs/git-worktree#_details
[^gitSubmoduleFile]: https://git-scm.com/docs/git-submodule#Documentation/git-submodule.txt-absorbgitdirs
[^codebergDomains]: https://docs.codeberg.org/codeberg-pages/using-custom-domain/
[^codebergRedirects]: https://docs.codeberg.org/codeberg-pages/redirects/

+
+// CleanDestinationDir configures the removal of stale files from the publishDir
+// when cleanDestinationDir is enabled.
+type CleanDestinationDir struct {
+	// Glob patterns matching files and directories, relative to the publishDir,
+	// that should never be removed, e.g. ".domains", "_redirects" or "**/.git" (the latter does not match a .git at the root).
+	// A matching directory is kept with all of its content.
+	Keep []string
+
+	compiledKeep []hstrings.Matcher
+}
+
+func (c *CleanDestinationDir) compileConfig() error {
+	c.compiledKeep = nil
+	for _, pattern := range c.Keep {
+		g, err := hglob.GetGlob(strings.TrimPrefix(filepath.ToSlash(pattern), "/"))
+		if err != nil {
+			return fmt.Errorf("failed to compile build.cleanDestinationDir.keep glob %q: %w", pattern, err)
+		}
+		c.compiledKeep = append(c.compiledKeep, g)
+	}
+	return nil
+}
+
+// ShouldKeep reports whether the file or directory at p, relative to the publishDir,
+// matches one of the Keep patterns.
+func (c CleanDestinationDir) ShouldKeep(p string) bool {
+	p = strings.TrimPrefix(filepath.ToSlash(p), "/")
+	for _, g := range c.compiledKeep {
+		if g.Match(p) {
+			return true
+		}
+	}
+	return false
 }

title: metrics: --templateMetrics duration columns have inconsistent formatting

judge.reasoning:
Both patches fix the issue the same way. Each adds a `formatDuration` helper that prints two fixed decimals with a fixed-width unit suffix and uses it for the sum/avg/max columns in both `WriteMetrics` branches. Each pads the unit so the decimal points align: Patch A uses "ns"/"µs"/"ms"/"s ", and Patch B uses " ns"/" µs"/" ms"/"  s". Go's fmt width counts runes, so the multi-byte µ does not break alignment in either one, and both are correct. Patch A also handles negative durations via `Abs`, which is harmless hardening.

The difference is in the tests and the side effects. Patch A keeps the value and unit adjacent, as before, so the existing duration-stripping regex in `partials_integration_test.go` still matches and no unrelated test needs changing. Patch B inserts a space between value and unit, which changes the output format and forces it to edit that integration test's regex. That is extra churn and a small risk for anything else that parses this output.

On tests, Patch A is stronger. It unit-tests `formatDuration`, including boundaries (0, exactly 1s, rounding). It also adds a `WriteMetrics` test, in both `calculateHints` modes, that checks the decimal point sits in the same rune column on every row for durations of mixed magnitude. That checks the issue's actual requirement and would fail against the old `Duration.String()` output. Patch B only unit-tests the helper with four values and never checks the table alignment.

One minor uncertainty: Patch A uses `strconv` without a visible import change, so it presumably relies on an existing import. Overall, Patch A is the more targeted and better-verified fix.

issue_md:
The `--templateMetrics` output table prints duration values (sum/avg/max) using `time.Duration.String()`, which varies both units and decimal places depending on the magnitude. This makes the table hard to scan when rows have durations of different magnitudes.

**Proposed fix:** Use a fixed-decimal formatter (two decimal places, unit suffix padded to consistent width) so decimal points align across all rows in the table.

title: Make .Render take additional data

judge.reasoning:
Both patches change the `Render` signature to `args ...any` the same way across the interface, the lazy provider, nopPage and testPage. When data is given, both pass it as the template context and otherwise fall back to the page. That is the issue's first option.

The difference is argument order. The issue writes the proposed form as `PAGE.Render [DATA] NAME`, with data before the name.

- Patch A accepts only `VIEW [CONTEXT]`. A call like `.Render (dict ...) "name"` fails in A with a cast error.
- Patch B accepts NAME, NAME DATA and DATA NAME. It finds the layout name by checking which argument is string-kinded, so it covers the issue's stated form and the alternative order. Its `reflect.Kind` check also accepts string types such as `template.HTML`.
- B has one ambiguity: when both arguments are strings, the first is treated as the name. That edge case would only bite string data in DATA-first order, and the doc comment documents the rule.

Tests:

- B's tests cover both orders, subdirectory views, scalar data, a safeHTML name, and error cases (no string argument, too many arguments, missing template).
- A's tests cover only name-first with a dict, plus two error cases.

B also updates the user docs for the new feature. That adds no risk.

Craft is comparable. B's `parseRenderArgs` helper is clean, and its error messages are informative.

On correctness against the issue's spec and on test breadth, B is the better fix.

issue_md:
See https://gohugo.io/methods/page/render/#article
See #15076

> PAGE.Render NAME

This has been discussed before. 

* The contract has always been that the templates that `.Renders` gets the data context as e.g. `page.html`, a `page.Page`.
* We can only pass 1 argument to Go's template renderer, which I guess is the blocking reason for not having done this sooner.

So, if we want to do:

> PAGE.Render [DATA] NAME

I'm guessing we have 2 top-level options:

* We say that if `DATA` is set, we use that as the context passed to the templates,. else `PAGE`.
* We somehow (e.g. by embeding it in a `{ DataAdditionalContext, Page }` struct or  putting it into the current `context.Context`) wrap the `Page` so you can do both `.RelPermalink` and `.DataAdditionalContext` (naming of the latter is just picked out of a hat without thinking too hard.

title: Add importContext to resources.Copy

judge.reasoning:
The issue asks for an `importContext` option on `resources.Copy`, with the signature changed to `resources.Copy [STRING or MAP] RESOURCE`. The context would be stored as internal state on the resource and honored by css.Build, js.Build/Batch, css.Sass and TailwindCSS.

Patch A implements exactly that. `resources.Copy` now accepts a target path, an options map, or nothing, and validates unknown options. An `ImportContext` is stored in an unexported field on `genericResource` and forwarded via `ResourceTransformationCtx.ImportContext`. It is consumed by:
- esbuild (js.Build/css.Build via `ApplyImportContext`)
- js.Batch, as a fallback through `InternalResourceImportContext`
- the PostCSS/Tailwind inline-import resolver
- Dart Sass
- LibSass

Patch A also handles cache correctness. The import context's key, including content hashes for in-memory resources, is folded into both the copy cache key and the resource `Key()`. Copies of the same resource with different contexts therefore don't collide, and a test covers this. Its tests are thorough and meaningful: CSS build with precedence and fallback to assets, JS build, cache separation, a Page as context, Mount, rebuild on edit, option validation, Dart Sass, LibSass, js.Batch, and unit tests for the resolver and getter. Docs are updated too.

Patch B does not touch `resources.Copy` at all, so the requested API is absent. Instead it adds `importContext` as an option to css.Build/js.Build, css.Sass (Dart) and TailwindCSS/PostCSS. To make those options hashable for transformation keys, it makes broad, risky changes:
- bumps `hashstructure` to v1.0.0 and rewrites hashing to use an UnwrapFunc
- removes `pageState.Key()` and adds `pageOutput.Key()`
- changes `Color.Hash` to `Key`
- changes `FromString` resource keys to include content hashes
- adds a new `testinginternal` template namespace exposed to all templates

These changes affect cache keys globally and add regression risk well beyond the issue. Its hash test hardcodes magic numbers, which is brittle. LibSass support is missing.

Patch A matches the issue's requested design, covers more transformers, and is better tested with less collateral risk.

title: Add css.ChromaStyles

judge.reasoning:
Both patches move the chromastyles generation logic out of commands/gen.go into a shared markup/highlight package, so the CLI and the new template function use the same code. Both add a css.ChromaStyles template function that returns a Resource.

Patch B follows the issue's explicit guidance that creating the Resource "should be delegated to `create.Client.FromString`". Patch A instead calls ResourceSpec.NewResource directly with a hand-rolled LazyPublish/Anonymous descriptor and its own small LRU cache. This duplicates what create.Client already does and adds risk around identity and dependency tracking and publishing semantics.

Patch B also handles the edges better:
- It copies the input map rather than decoding it in place, so site params used as options are not mutated, and a test asserts this.
- It normalizes targetPath with paths.ToSlashTrimLeading.
- It rejects unknown option keys, such as the typo `styel`, with a clear error.
- It prefixes errors with `css.ChromaStyles:`.

Patch A has one nice touch: it defaults the style to the markup.highlight.style config value, which arguably fits the "configured in hugo.toml" wish. Patch B defaults to `friendly`, but its documentation shows config-driven options via site.Params, which also meets that wish.

On tests, Patch B adds both unit tests for the shared package (decoding, mode selector, highlight style, error cases) and integration tests (params-sourced options, map immutability, error cases including a non-map argument). Patch A has integration and error tests plus a benchmark but no unit coverage of the shared code. Patch B also adds documentation.

Overall, Patch B is more faithful to the issue's design direction, more robust, and better tested.

issue_md:
We have a [CLI command](https://gohugo.io/commands/hugo_gen_chromastyles/#hugo-gen-chromastyles) for this, with Chroma's recent addition of dark/light modes, it would be convenient to generate these on-the-fly. This would allow this to be configured in `hugo.toml` and also allow the user an easier way to find the correct settings.

E.g.

```handlebars
{{ $dark := css.ChromaStyles dict 
  "targetPath" "css/croma_dark.css"
   "style" "monokai"
   "modeSelector" "dark"
    "mode" "dark"
}}
<link rel="stylesheet" href="{{ $dark.RelPermalink }}">
```

This would be even more useful if we fix #15103.


* The options would be `targetPath` + the options in https://gohugo.io/commands/hugo_gen_chromastyles/#hugo-gen-chromastyles
* Some sharing of code between the gen command in the commands package would be sensible.
* Creating the `Resource` should be delegated to `create.Client.FromString`.

+---
+title: css.ChromaStyles
+description: Returns a CSS resource with the syntax highlighting styles for the Chroma code highlighter.
+categories: []
+keywords: []
+params:
+  functions_and_methods:
+    aliases: []
+    returnType: resource.Resource
+    signatures: ['css.ChromaStyles OPTIONS']
+---
+
+The `css.ChromaStyles` function generates a CSS stylesheet for the [Chroma](https://github.com/alecthomas/chroma) code highlighter, the same as the [`hugo gen chromastyles`](/commands/hugo_gen_chromastyles/) command. The stylesheet is needed if `markup.highlight.noClasses` is disabled in your project configuration.
+
+```go-html-template
+{{ $dark := css.ChromaStyles (dict
+  "targetPath" "css/chroma_dark.css"
+  "style" "github"
+  "mode" "dark"
+  "modeSelector" true
+) }}
+<link rel="stylesheet" href="{{ $dark.RelPermalink }}">
+```
+
+The options map can also come from your project configuration, e.g. `{{ css.ChromaStyles site.Params.chroma.dark }}`.
+
+## Options
+
+targetPath
+: (`string`) The publish path of the stylesheet, relative to the root of the published site. Required.
+
+style
+: (`string`) The Chroma style name. See the [syntax highlighting styles](/quick-reference/syntax-highlighting-styles/) for a preview of the available styles. Default is `friendly`.
+
+mode
+: (`string`) The style mode, either `light` or `dark`. Default is the style's own mode.
+
+modeSelector
+: (`bool`) Whether to scope every selector under a top level mode class, e.g. `.dark .chroma`. This allows you to include both a light and a dark stylesheet and toggle them with a class on a parent element. Default is `false`.
+
+highlightStyle
+: (`string`) The foreground and background colors for highlighted lines, e.g. `#fff000 bg:#000fff`.
+
+lineNumbersInlineStyle
+: (`string`) The foreground and background colors for inline line numbers, e.g. `#fff000 bg:#000fff`.
+
+lineNumbersTableStyle
+: (`string`) The foreground and background colors for table line numbers, e.g. `#fff000 bg:#000fff`.
+
+omitClassComments
+: (`bool`) Whether to omit the CSS class comment prefixes in the generated CSS. Default is `false`.

@@ -0,0 +1,201 @@

+// Package chromastyles generates CSS stylesheets for the Chroma code highlighter.
+// It is shared by the "hugo gen chromastyles" command and the css.ChromaStyles template function.
+package chromastyles
+
+import (
+	"bytes"
+	"fmt"
+	"io"
+	"slices"
+	"strings"
+
+	"github.com/alecthomas/chroma/v2"
+	"github.com/alecthomas/chroma/v2/formatters/html"
+	"github.com/alecthomas/chroma/v2/styles"
+	"github.com/mitchellh/mapstructure"
+)
+
+// DefaultStyle is the style used when none is set.
+const DefaultStyle = "friendly"
+
+// Options configures the generated stylesheet.
+type Options struct {
+	// The Chroma style name, e.g. "monokai".
+	Style string
+
+	// The style mode, "light" or "dark". Empty means the style's default.
+	Mode string
+
+	// Whether to scope every selector under a top level mode class, e.g. ".dark .chroma".
+	ModeSelector bool
+
+	// Foreground and background colors for highlighted lines, e.g. "#fff000 bg:#000fff".
+	HighlightStyle string
+
+	// Foreground and background colors for inline line numbers, e.g. "#fff000 bg:#000fff".
+	LineNumbersInlineStyle string
+
+	// Foreground and background colors for table line numbers, e.g. "#fff000 bg:#000fff".
+	LineNumbersTableStyle string
+
+	// Whether to omit the CSS class comment prefixes.
+	OmitClassComments bool
+}
+
+// DecodeOptions decodes m into Options, applying defaults.
+func DecodeOptions(m map[string]any) (Options, error) {
+	opts := Options{Style: DefaultStyle}
+	if m == nil {
+		return opts, nil
+	}
+	var md mapstructure.Metadata
+	if err := mapstructure.WeakDecodeMetadata(m, &opts, &md); err != nil {
+		return opts, fmt.Errorf("failed to decode chroma styles options: %w", err)
+	}
+	if len(md.Unused) > 0 {
+		slices.Sort(md.Unused)
+		return opts, fmt.Errorf("unknown chroma styles option(s): %s", strings.Join(md.Unused, ", "))
+	}
+	return opts, nil
+}
+
+// Write writes the CSS stylesheet for the given options to w.
+func Write(w io.Writer, opts Options) error {
+	styleName := strings.ToLower(opts.Style)
+	if styleName == "" {
+		styleName = DefaultStyle
+	}
+	if !slices.Contains(styles.Names(), styleName) {
+		return fmt.Errorf("invalid style: %s", styleName)
+	}
+
+	var chromaStyle *chroma.Style
+	if opts.Mode != "" {
+		var chromaMode chroma.Mode
+		switch opts.Mode {
+		case "light":
+			chromaMode = chroma.Light
+		case "dark":
+			chromaMode = chroma.Dark
+		default:
+			return fmt.Errorf("invalid mode: %s", opts.Mode)
+		}
+
+		chromaStyle = styles.GetForMode(styleName, chromaMode)
+		if chromaStyle.Mode() != chromaMode {
+			return fmt.Errorf("style %q does not have a %q mode", styleName, opts.Mode)
+		}
+	} else {
+		chromaStyle = styles.Get(styleName)
+	}
+
+	builder := chromaStyle.Builder()
+	if opts.HighlightStyle != "" {
+		builder.Add(chroma.LineHighlight, opts.HighlightStyle)
+	}
+	if opts.LineNumbersInlineStyle != "" {
+		builder.Add(chroma.LineNumbers, opts.LineNumbersInlineStyle)
+	}
+	if opts.LineNumbersTableStyle != "" {
+		builder.Add(chroma.LineNumbersTable, opts.LineNumbersTableStyle)
+	}
+	style, err := builder.Build()
+	if err != nil {
+		return err
+	}
+
+	htmlOptions := []html.Option{
+		html.WithCSSComments(!opts.OmitClassComments),
+	}
+	if !opts.ModeSelector {
+		// Only needed for the shared-scope overlay; ModeSelector
+		// gives each mode its own scope and makes this redundant.
+		htmlOptions = append(htmlOptions, html.WithCustomCSS(cssOverrides(style)))
+	}
+
+	formatter := html.New(htmlOptions...)
+
+	if !opts.ModeSelector {
+		return formatter.WriteCSS(w, style)
+	}
+
+	// Scope every selector under a top level mode class, e.g. ".dark .chroma".
+	// This allows generating both light and dark stylesheets and toggling
+	// them with a parent class on the page.
+	// There's no upstream option for this (I think), so do string replacements for now.
+	// TODO(bep) upstream option for this.
+	var prefix string
+	switch style.Mode() {
+	case chroma.Light:
+		prefix = ".light "
+	case chroma.Dark:
+		prefix = ".dark "
+	default:
+		return fmt.Errorf("style %q does not have a %q mode", style.Name, opts.Mode)
+	}
+
+	var buf bytes.Buffer
+	if err := formatter.WriteCSS(&buf, style); err != nil {
+		return err
+	}
+	replacer := strings.NewReplacer(
+		".bg {", prefix+".bg {",
+		".chroma ", prefix+".chroma ",
+	)
+	_, err = replacer.WriteString(w, buf.String())
+	return err
+}
+
+// String returns the CSS stylesheet for the given options.
+func String(opts Options) (string, error) {
+	var buf bytes.Buffer
+	if err := Write(&buf, opts); err != nil {
+		return "", err
+	}
+	return buf.String(), nil
+}
+
+// cssOverrides re-emits leaf token colors that Chroma's minifier drops
+// because they equal the style's default foreground (the .chroma color). Without
+// mode selector scoping, a paired light/dark stylesheet shares the same .chroma
+// scope, and the light sheet's explicit rule (e.g. .chroma .nx) would otherwise
+// leak into dark mode, since an explicit declaration beats inheritance.
+func cssOverrides(style *chroma.Style) map[chroma.TokenType]string {
+	bg := style.Get(chroma.Background)
+	m := make(map[chroma.TokenType]string)
+	for tt := range chroma.StandardTypes {
+		if tt == chroma.Background || !style.Has(tt) || !leafToken(tt) {
+			continue
+		}
+		entry := style.Get(tt)
+		if !entry.Sub(bg).IsZero() || !entry.Colour.IsSet() {
+			continue
+		}
+		if css := html.StyleEntryToCSS(chroma.StyleEntry{Colour: entry.Colour}); css != "" {
+			m[tt] = css
+		}
+	}
+	return m
+}
+
+func leafToken(tt chroma.TokenType) bool {
+	for other := range chroma.StandardTypes {
+		if other != tt && (other.Category() == tt || other.SubCategory() == tt) {
+			return false
+		}
+	}
+	return true
+}

+
+func TestDecodeOptions(t *testing.T) {
+	c := qt.New(t)
+
+	opts, err := DecodeOptions(nil)
+	c.Assert(err, qt.IsNil)
+	c.Assert(opts, qt.Equals, Options{Style: DefaultStyle})
+
+	opts, err = DecodeOptions(map[string]any{
+		"style":                  "monokai",
+		"mode":                   "dark",
+		"modeselector":           "true",
+		"highlightStyle":         "#fff000 bg:#000fff",
+		"lineNumbersInlineStyle": "#aaa",
+		"lineNumbersTableStyle":  "#bbb",
+		"omitClassComments":      true,
+	})
+	c.Assert(err, qt.IsNil)
+	c.Assert(opts, qt.Equals, Options{
+		Style:                  "monokai",
+		Mode:                   "dark",
+		ModeSelector:           true,
+		HighlightStyle:         "#fff000 bg:#000fff",
+		LineNumbersInlineStyle: "#aaa",
+		LineNumbersTableStyle:  "#bbb",
+		OmitClassComments:      true,
+	})
+
+	_, err = DecodeOptions(map[string]any{"styel": "monokai"})
+	c.Assert(err, qt.ErrorMatches, `unknown chroma styles option\(s\): styel`)
+}
+
+func TestString(t *testing.T) {
+	c := qt.New(t)
+
+	css, err := String(Options{Style: "monokai"})
+	c.Assert(err, qt.IsNil)
+	c.Assert(css, qt.Contains, "/* GenericSubheading */")
+	c.Assert(css, qt.Contains, ".chroma ")
+	c.Assert(css, qt.Not(qt.Contains), ".dark ")
+
+	css, err = String(Options{Style: "monokai", OmitClassComments: true})
+	c.Assert(err, qt.IsNil)
+	c.Assert(css, qt.Not(qt.Contains), "GenericSubheading")
+
+	// Same-colour leaf token classes are kept without mode selector.
+	css, err = String(Options{Style: "github-dark"})
+	c.Assert(err, qt.IsNil)
+	c.Assert(css, qt.Matches, `(?s).*\.chroma \.nx \{ color:#e6edf3 \}.*`)
+
+	css, err = String(Options{Style: "github", Mode: "dark", ModeSelector: true})
+	c.Assert(err, qt.IsNil)
+	c.Assert(css, qt.Contains, ".dark .chroma ")
+	c.Assert(css, qt.Contains, ".dark .bg {")
+
+	css, err = String(Options{Style: "github", Mode: "light", ModeSelector: true})
+	c.Assert(err, qt.IsNil)
+	c.Assert(css, qt.Contains, ".light .chroma ")
+
+	css, err = String(Options{Style: "ashen", ModeSelector: true})
+	c.Assert(err, qt.IsNil)
+	c.Assert(css, qt.Contains, ".dark .chroma ")
+
+	css, err = String(Options{Style: "monokai", HighlightStyle: "#fff000 bg:#000fff"})
+	c.Assert(err, qt.IsNil)
+	c.Assert(css, qt.Matches, `(?s).*\.chroma \.hl \{[^}]*#000fff.*`)
+
+	_, err = String(Options{Style: "__invalid_style__"})
+	c.Assert(err, qt.ErrorMatches, `invalid style: __invalid_style__`)
+
+	_, err = String(Options{Style: "github", Mode: "dim"})
+	c.Assert(err, qt.ErrorMatches, `invalid mode: dim`)
+
+	_, err = String(Options{Style: "friendly", Mode: "dark"})
+	c.Assert(err, qt.ErrorMatches, `style "friendly" does not have a "dark" mode`)

@@ -0,0 +1,161 @@
+// Copyright 2026 The Hugo Authors. All rights reserved.
+//

+// limitations under the License.
+
+package highlight
+
+import (
+	"bytes"
+	"fmt"
+	"slices"
+	"strings"
+
+	"github.com/alecthomas/chroma/v2"
+	"github.com/alecthomas/chroma/v2/formatters/html"
+	"github.com/alecthomas/chroma/v2/styles"
+)
+
+// ChromaStylesOptions holds options for ChromaStylesCSS.
+type ChromaStylesOptions struct {
+	// Highlighter style, e.g. "monokai".
+	Style string
+
+	// Style mode, "light" or "dark".
+	Mode string
+
+	// Scope selectors under a top level mode class, e.g. ".dark .chroma".
+	ModeSelector bool
+
+	// Foreground and background colors for highlighted lines, e.g. "#fff000 bg:#000fff".
+	HighlightStyle string
+
+	// Foreground and background colors for inline line numbers.
+	LineNumbersInlineStyle string
+
+	// Foreground and background colors for table line numbers.
+	LineNumbersTableStyle string
+
+	// Omit CSS class comment prefixes in the generated CSS.
+	OmitClassComments bool
+}
+
+// ChromaStylesCSS generates a CSS stylesheet for the Chroma code highlighter.
+// This stylesheet is needed if markup.highlight.noClasses is disabled in config.
+func ChromaStylesCSS(opts ChromaStylesOptions) (string, error) {
+	name := strings.ToLower(opts.Style)
+	if !slices.Contains(styles.Names(), name) {
+		return "", fmt.Errorf("invalid style: %s", name)
+	}
+	var chromaStyle *chroma.Style
+	if opts.Mode != "" {
+		var mode chroma.Mode
+		switch opts.Mode {
+		case "light":
+			mode = chroma.Light
+		case "dark":
+			mode = chroma.Dark
+		default:
+			return "", fmt.Errorf("invalid mode: %s", opts.Mode)
+		}
+
+		chromaStyle = styles.GetForMode(name, mode)
+		if chromaStyle.Mode() != mode {
+			return "", fmt.Errorf("style %q does not have a %q mode", name, opts.Mode)
+		}
+	} else {
+		chromaStyle = styles.Get(name)
+	}
+	builder := chromaStyle.Builder()
+	if opts.HighlightStyle != "" {
+		builder.Add(chroma.LineHighlight, opts.HighlightStyle)
+	}
+	if opts.LineNumbersInlineStyle != "" {
+		builder.Add(chroma.LineNumbers, opts.LineNumbersInlineStyle)
+	}
+	if opts.LineNumbersTableStyle != "" {
+		builder.Add(chroma.LineNumbersTable, opts.LineNumbersTableStyle)
+	}
+	style, err := builder.Build()
+	if err != nil {
+		return "", err
+	}
+
+	options := []html.Option{
+		html.WithCSSComments(!opts.OmitClassComments),
+	}
+	if !opts.ModeSelector {
+		// Only needed for the shared-scope overlay; modeSelector
+		// gives each mode its own scope and makes this redundant.
+		options = append(options, html.WithCustomCSS(chromaCSSOverrides(style)))
+	}
+
+	var buf bytes.Buffer
+	if err := html.New(options...).WriteCSS(&buf, style); err != nil {
+		return "", err
+	}
+	css := buf.String()
+	if opts.ModeSelector {
+		// Scope every selector under a top level mode class, e.g. ".dark .chroma".
+		// This allows generating both light and dark stylesheets and toggling
+		// them with a parent class on the page.
+		// There's no upstream option for this (I think), so do string replacements for now.
+		// TODO(bep) upstream option for this.
+		var prefix string
+		switch style.Mode() {
+		case chroma.Light:
+			prefix = ".light "
+		case chroma.Dark:
+			prefix = ".dark "
+		default:
+			return "", fmt.Errorf("style %q does not have a light or dark mode", style.Name)
+		}
+		replacer := strings.NewReplacer(
+			".bg {", prefix+".bg {",
+			".chroma ", prefix+".chroma ",
+		)
+		css = replacer.Replace(css)
+	}
+
+	return css, nil
+}
+
+// chromaCSSOverrides re-emits leaf token colors that Chroma's minifier drops
+// because they equal the style's default foreground (the .chroma color). Without
+// modeSelector scoping, a paired light/dark stylesheet shares the same .chroma
+// scope, and the light sheet's explicit rule (e.g. .chroma .nx) would otherwise
+// leak into dark mode, since an explicit declaration beats inheritance.
+func chromaCSSOverrides(style *chroma.Style) map[chroma.TokenType]string {
+	bg := style.Get(chroma.Background)
+	m := make(map[chroma.TokenType]string)
+	for tt := range chroma.StandardTypes {
+		if tt == chroma.Background || !style.Has(tt) || !chromaLeafToken(tt) {
+			continue
+		}
+		entry := style.Get(tt)
+		if !entry.Sub(bg).IsZero() || !entry.Colour.IsSet() {
+			continue
+		}
+		if css := html.StyleEntryToCSS(chroma.StyleEntry{Colour: entry.Colour}); css != "" {
+			m[tt] = css
+		}
+	}
+	return m
+}
+
+func chromaLeafToken(tt chroma.TokenType) bool {
+	for other := range chroma.StandardTypes {
+		if other != tt && (other.Category() == tt || other.SubCategory() == tt) {
+			return false
+		}
+	}
+	return true
+}

title: common/hugo: Include aom, dav1d, and libavif in commands/env output

judge.reasoning: Patch A does exactly what the issue asks. It adds libavif v1.4.1, aom v3.14.1 and dav1d 1.5.3 to GetDependencyListNonGo next to libwebp, and adds a comment pointing to the Makefiles that must stay in sync. It also adds a unit test (TestGetDependencyListNonGo) and updates the env testscript to check the exact version strings. Both tests would fail before the change and pass after. Patch B tries a more structural approach: it moves the versions into internal/warpc constants and makes common/hugo import internal/warpc. That brings in real risk. common/hugo is a low-level package, and warpc is a heavier internal package with many dependencies, so this new import could create an import cycle or an undesirable dependency direction. Patch B also goes beyond the ask: it adds a KaTeX entry whose hardcoded version (0.16.21) cannot be checked against anything in the diff, and it reorders libwebp in the output. It also includes unrelated formatting churn in warpc.go (parenthesis/argument reformatting) that obscures the fix. Its testscript checks only module paths, not versions, so its tests are weaker. Patch B still hardcodes the versions as constants, so the claimed single source of truth gains little over Patch A's comment. Patch A is correct, minimal, better tested, and lower risk.

title: resources/jsconfig: Address VS Code linting notice in jsconfig.json

judge.reasoning: Patch A fixes the root cause. The VS Code notice fires because a mapping target is non-relative while baseUrl is unset. Patch A prefixes './' to every generated target that does not already start with '../', so all source roots become valid relative mappings. That includes the reported "*": ["*"] case, which becomes "./*", and nested roots like 'c/*', which become './c/*'. The '*' mapping is kept, so editors can still resolve non-relative imports such as 'js/util.js' from the assets directory. Without baseUrl, removing that mapping would leave those imports unresolved. Patch B instead skips the source root equal to the config directory. For the single-root example this makes Build return nil, so the lint warning goes away only because the mapping is gone, and the import-resolution benefit is lost with it. B also leaves the problem in place for any other root under the directory: Build('/a/b') with root '/a/b/c' still emits the non-relative 'c/*'. On tests, A adds a unit test covering same-dir, child and parent roots, plus an integration test that checks the exact jsconfig.json content. Both would fail before the fix. B adds only a nil-config assertion for the single-root case. Both patches are small in scope. A wins on correctness and on test coverage.

title: Panic when deleting a directory in static when server is running

judge.reasoning:
Both patches stop the panic in processPartialFileEvents, but B is the more contained and better-tested fix.

Patch B filters static-component paths out of the resolved component paths before any per-path processing. Static files then never reach the switch or any later logic in the build-graph code. The comment states the right reason: static files are handled by the static syncer, not the site build. Because the filter works per component path, a file mounted into both static and assets still triggers an asset rebuild. B tests exactly that dual-mount case.

B's tests use the in-process TestRunning harness. They cover removing a directory (the issue's scenario), renaming a directory, removing a file, adding and editing a file, and the dual static/assets mount. Each would hit the panic before the fix and pass after. They also assert that nothing is rendered and that later edits still rebuild correctly.

Patch A adds a `case files.ComponentFolderStatic` no-op to the switch, which fixes the panic. It also rewrites `SourceFilesystem.Contains` to use `ReverseLookup`. That change goes beyond the issue: it alters how the static syncer decides whether a path belongs to a filesystem, now including file mounts that were previously skipped. It may be a legitimate improvement, but it adds behavioral risk in code shared by other callers and is not needed for the reported panic.

A's tests are server testscripts with sleeps and a check for empty stderr. They exercise the real server path but are timing-dependent. Both use custom mounts rather than the plain static-directory deletion described in the issue.

Overall, B fixes the root symptom precisely, guards the edge cases, and has stronger, deterministic tests with no unrelated churn.

title: related: Add option to tokenize headings

judge.reasoning:
Patch B is the more correct and better-contained fix.

Patch B:
- Keeps the existing identifier-based `FragmentKeyword` entries and adds heading-word tokens alongside them. Exact identifier matching still works, including explicit `fragments` in search options and `fragmentrefs` pointing at heading IDs; its test covers this with p4/p5.
- Uses a distinct `headingTokenKeyword` type, so a word can never collide with a fragment ID.
- Makes `applyFilter` work with tokens: the type switch in `searchDate` collects token keywords, and `headingMatchesTokens` re-tokenizes heading titles for the filter.
- Tokenizes only heading titles, as the issue specifies. Definition terms keep exact matching, and a test asserts this.
- Handles HTML in titles by stripping tags and unescaping entities, and keeps Unicode combining marks inside words.
- Updates the docs with the exact wording from the issue.
- Tests cover both tokenize=true and tokenize=false, plus config decoding and the tokenizer itself.

Patch A has real correctness problems:
- When tokenize is on, it `continue`s past headings, so it no longer indexes their fragment identifiers. This silently breaks exact fragment-ID matching, for example `Related` with `fragments` options or `fragmentrefs` targeting headings.
- Its tokens are created with `stringToKeyword`, which produces `StringKeyword`. But the `applyFilter` path in `searchDate` only collects `kw.(FragmentKeyword)`, so `ff.words` is never populated. Heading filtering with tokenize therefore does not work as intended, and its own ApplyFilter test looks unlikely to pass for the right reason.
- It expands scope beyond the issue: tokenization for basic indices through `ToKeywords`, plus a new `MinTokenLength` option. This adds risk without being asked for.
- It adds no documentation and includes whitespace churn in an existing test file.

On correctness, scope and tests, B is clearly better.

issue_md:
See <https://discourse.gohugo.io/t/related-posts-based-on-heading/57467>.

I suggest using the name `tokenize`, documented as follows:

> (`bool`) Whether to split multi-word values into individual keywords for indexing and matching. title: panic: slice bounds out of range in contentNodeShifter.Delete when removing draft pages from a multilingual taxonomy
issue_md:
### What version of Hugo are you using?

Reproduced on both:

```
hugo v0.159.1-86c7d3afacab79dc53325602d77ef884b7570268+extended darwin/arm64
hugo v0.164.0+extended+withdeploy darwin/arm64
```

### Does this issue reproduce with the latest release?

Yes (0.164.0).

### What did you expect to see?

A production build (no `-D`) of a multilingual site containing draft pages completes.

### What did you see instead?

```
panic: runtime error: slice bounds out of range [5:4]

goroutine 37 [running]:
github.com/gohugoio/hugo/hugolib.(*contentNodeShifter).Delete(0x..., {0x..., 0x...}, {0x2, 0x0, 0x0})
	github.com/gohugoio/hugo/hugolib/content_map_page_contentnodeshifter.go:48 +0x5f4
github.com/gohugoio/hugo/hugolib/doctree.(*NodeShiftTree[...]).delete(0x..., {0x..., 0x35})
	github.com/gohugoio/hugo/hugolib/doctree/nodeshifttree.go:165 +0x84
github.com/gohugoio/hugo/hugolib/doctree.(*NodeShiftTree[...]).Delete(...)
	github.com/gohugoio/hugo/hugolib/doctree/nodeshifttree.go:107
github.com/gohugoio/hugo/hugolib.(*allPagesAssembler).createAllPages.func1-range1(...)
	github.com/gohugoio/hugo/hugolib/content_map_page_assembler.go:106 +0xa4
github.com/gohugoio/hugo/hugolib.(*allPagesAssembler).createAllPages(...)
	github.com/gohugoio/hugo/hugolib/content_map_page_assembler.go:138 +0x168
github.com/gohugoio/hugo/hugolib.(*HugoSites).assemble(...)
	github.com/gohugoio/hugo/hugolib/hugo_sites_build.go:345 +0x41c
```

The `0x35` in `delete(..., {…, 0x35})` is 53, exactly the byte length of the key being removed (`/blog/` plus a 47-character slug).

### Only on the page-removal path

`hugo -D` (drafts included) builds fine. The panic appears only when a page is *removed* from the tree, which makes it invisible in local preview and fatal only in production.

A **future `publishDate`** panics identically. Setting `[_build] render = "never"` / `list = "never"` on the same pages avoids it entirely — consistent with those pages never being added to the tree, so nothing is deleted.

### What I ruled out

Site: 8 languages, ~1,490 pages per language, ~11,455 content files, `categories` taxonomy.

- **Not a regression.** 0.159.1 and 0.164.0 behave identically.
- **Not the number of drafts.** 96 draft pages build fine; 16 panic.
- **Not slug length.** The panicking key was 47 chars, but renaming an unrelated post to exactly 47 chars builds fine.
- **Not the slug.** Renaming the offending page does not help.
- **Not byte layout.** Deleting a front-matter line, or adding a blank one, still panics.

Swapping page *content* at a fixed path isolates it to **front matter**. Changing `categories = ["Airport Operations"]` on the offending page to any other value clears the panic — and so does moving a *different* page out of that same category while leaving the offending one alone. So the trigger is combinatorial: some particular set of pages being deleted from one taxonomy term corrupts the shifter, rather than any single page being malformed.

### Reproducer

I have not managed to minimise it, and I want to be upfront about that. Synthetic multilingual sites (8 languages, 12 blog + 200 glossary pages sharing one taxonomy term, varying draft counts) do **not** reproduce, so something else in the real tree is required. The affected repository is private.

I am happy to run patches or instrumented builds against the real site and report back, which may be faster than guessing at a minimal case.

title: Add resources.Publish

judge.reasoning:
Both patches implement the same core fix. Each adds `Namespace.Publish(r resource.Resource)`, which type-asserts to `resource.Source`, calls `Publish()` and returns `r`. Both register the method mapping in `init.go`. So correctness is essentially equal and both resolve the issue's ask, letting `{{ ... | js.Build | resources.Publish }}` work.

The difference is mainly in testing. Patch B's single test covers one minified JS resource and checks that the file is written. Patch A's test covers a much wider range of resource kinds:
- a transformed JS resource
- a plain global CSS resource
- `resources.FromString`
- an image
- a resized image
- a page bundle resource when `publishResources` is false, with a negative check that a sibling resource is not published

Patch A also adds a failure-path test confirming that passing a non-resource produces a sensible error. These tests would fail before the change, because the function is missing from the namespace, and they exercise more real-world scenarios.

On craft, Patch A adds an explicit nil check and prefixes its error messages with `resources.Publish:`, which makes template errors clearer. Its doc comment shows the intended pipeline usage. The documentation page is extra scope but harmless and appropriate for a new template function.

One small risk is whether `errors` is already imported in `resources.go`; neither diff shows import changes, so I treat this as neutral. Overall Patch A is the stronger, better-tested fix.

title: Upgrade to Go 1.27

judge.reasoning: Both patches make the core version bumps: CI, CircleCI image, go.mod and Dockerfile GO_VERSION. Both also pull in the same main upstream template-package changes: the CVE fix for JS regexp context after braces in transition.go, delimiter-aware node String/writeTo, the stringer bounds fixes and the Funcs doc changes. The difference is in what else a Go 1.27 upgrade needs to actually build and pass tests. Patch A covers several runtime and test breakages that Patch B ignores. (1) In warpc, it tolerates ErrShutdown from inGroup.Wait(). The comment says Go 1.27's json/v2 Decode now surfaces read errors on closed pipes, so without this, dispatcher shutdown would return errors. (2) It adds a mutex around wazero compilation-cache creation to fix a data race. (3) It regenerates the image golden files, which suggests image output changed under the new toolchain; without them the image tests would fail. (4) It does a fuller template sync. It removes the obsolete `// +build` lines and the go1.13 build constraints from the forked test files; that constraint sets the file language version to 1.13, which Patch B's own comment says breaks newer syntax, yet B leaves those constraints in the existing files. It brings in the upstream testenv_unix changes and the new TestExecError_CustomError. It also hardens the fork script: a skip hook so the stubbed testenv.go is preserved (backed by a real fix in hugio.CopyDir, which previously ignored shouldCopy for files), the godebug-stripping replacers for escape.go, and the validateType rename. Patch B instead hand-edits testenv.go, which the next fork run would overwrite. Patch A has some churn: herrors.Or replacing cmp.Or, a simplified readFileFromFs, lint-ignore comments, and some non-gofmt formatting in the synced tests that mirrors upstream. Patch B's extras are a README bump, a snap channel pin and a nice Hugo-level integration test for the CVE. Patch B's integration test is a plus, but it does not offset its missing coverage of the shutdown-error and golden-image breakages. Patch A is the more complete and correct upgrade.

title: templates.Defer: identical block bodies in different output formats share one escaping mode, chosen non-deterministically per build

judge.reasoning:
Both patches fix the root cause the issue identifies. Each puts the owner's plain-text/HTML mode into the deferred template ID. That separates HTML and plain-text registrations while keeping same-mode sharing, which the documented key-plus-content-hash cache relies on.

The patches differ at one edge. Patch B reads `c.t.D.IsPlainText` from whatever template the transform context currently belongs to. Inside a partial-decorator body, `handleWithPartial` creates a nested context whose `t` is the decorator partial (e.g. `d.html`), not the owner. Patch A's comments say the collected defer nodes are registered under the owner. If so, under B a deferred block inside a decorator in a plain-text owner gets the HTML-mode ID. It is then parsed under the owner's mode and can still collide with an identical HTML-owner body. Patch A avoids this by adding a `deferPlainText` flag that is set from the owner and passed explicitly into the nested decorator context. It covers this case with its own test (`TestDeferInPartialDecoratorInPlainTextOutputFormat`).

Patch A's tests are also stronger:
- It builds 10 times per scenario, which addresses the order-dependent flakiness. B's single build could pass by luck before the fix.
- It covers both the same-key and different-key variants from the issue.
- It adds a regression test showing that same-format identical bodies still share one execution, the constraint the issue spells out.

Patch A's prefix-outside-the-hash approach is also slightly cleaner than B's `fmt.Sprintf` into the hashed string. B also relies on `fmt` already being imported in that file, which the diff does not show.

Overall, Patch A is more correct at the edge and better tested.

issue_md:
### What version of Hugo are you using (`hugo version`)? 
$ hugo version
hugo v0.164.0-ce2470e7012b5ab5fc4e10ebe4027e9f8d9e00dc+extended windows/amd64 BuildDate=2026-07-06T16:39:30Z VendorInfo=gohugoio
### Does this issue reproduce with the latest release? Yes. ```text hugo v0.165.0-76a5e1880ab46688155b02e99bab9be2a6134492+extended windows/amd64 BuildDate=2026-08-12T14:26:28Z VendorInfo=gohugoio ``` Over one run of 40 consecutive builds of the unchanged reproduction site below with that binary, 28 builds published the wrong value in `public/index.html` and 12 published the wrong value in `public/index.txt`. All 40 exited 0, and none printed a warning or an error. ### Summary When two templates belonging to different output formats contain byte-identical `templates.Defer` block bodies, both blocks do execute, each with its own correct output-format context. What they share is the escaping applied inside the block, and which of the two escaping modes survives changes from build to build of an unchanged site. On every build exactly one of the two outputs is therefore wrong: either an HTML page publishes a value raw that it escapes correctly a few characters earlier outside the block, or a plain-text page receives HTML entities. ### Reproduction Three files in an empty directory. No content, no modules, no external tooling. `hugo.toml`: ```toml baseURL = 'https://example.org/' title = 'defer probe' disableKinds = ['page', 'section', 'taxonomy', 'term', 'RSS', 'sitemap', 'robotsTXT'] [outputFormats.probe] mediaType = 'text/plain' baseName = 'index' isPlainText = true [outputs] home = ['html', 'probe'] ``` `layouts/home.html`: ```go-html-template {{ $v := "&" }}OUT[{{ $v }}]{{ with (templates.Defer (dict "key" "K" "data" (dict "v" $v))) }}IN[{{ .v }}]{{ end }} ``` `layouts/home.probe.txt`, byte-identical to `layouts/home.html` (both md5 `c921197a9c8637852e38d94a0352359d`): ```go-html-template {{ $v := "&" }}OUT[{{ $v }}]{{ with (templates.Defer (dict "key" "K" "data" (dict "v" $v))) }}IN[{{ .v }}]{{ end }} ``` `OUT[...]` interpolates the value outside the deferred block, `IN[...]` interpolates the same value inside it. Then run `hugo` several times without changing anything, and look at `public/index.html` and `public/index.txt` after each run. ### What happens Two consecutive runs of the same command on the unchanged site, pasted verbatim: ```text $ hugo --logLevel info Start building sites … hugo v0.164.0-ce2470e7012b5ab5fc4e10ebe4027e9f8d9e00dc+extended windows/amd64 BuildDate=2026-07-06T16:39:30Z VendorInfo=gohugoio INFO build: step process substep collect files 0 files_total 0 pagesources_total 0 resourcesources_total 0 duration 0s INFO build: step process duration 0s INFO build: step assemble duration 0s INFO build: step render substep pages site en outputFormat html duration 1.3703ms INFO build: step render substep pages site en outputFormat probe duration 509.5µs INFO build: step render pages 2 content 0 duration 1.8798ms INFO build: step render deferred count 2 duration 1.7766ms INFO build: step postProcess duration 0s INFO build: duration 4.171ms │ EN ──────────────────┼──── Pages │ 2 Paginator pages │ 0 Non-page files │ 0 Static files │ 0 Processed images │ 0 Aliases │ 0 Cleaned │ 0 Total in 12 ms --- public/index.html --- OUT[<b>&]IN[&] --- public/index.txt --- OUT[&]IN[&] ``` ```text $ hugo --logLevel info Start building sites … hugo v0.164.0-ce2470e7012b5ab5fc4e10ebe4027e9f8d9e00dc+extended windows/amd64 BuildDate=2026-07-06T16:39:30Z VendorInfo=gohugoio INFO build: step process substep collect files 0 files_total 0 pagesources_total 0 resourcesources_total 0 duration 513.8µs INFO build: step process duration 513.8µs INFO build: step assemble duration 0s INFO build: step render substep pages site en outputFormat html duration 517.9µs INFO build: step render substep pages site en outputFormat probe duration 517.2µs INFO build: step render pages 2 content 0 duration 1.0351ms INFO build: step render deferred count 2 duration 2.0736ms INFO build: step postProcess duration 0s INFO build: duration 3.6225ms │ EN ──────────────────┼──── Pages │ 2 Paginator pages │ 0 Non-page files │ 0 Static files │ 0 Processed images │ 0 Aliases │ 0 Cleaned │ 0 Total in 12 ms --- public/index.html --- OUT[<b>&]IN[<b>&] --- public/index.txt --- OUT[&]IN[<b>&] ``` In the first run the HTML page publishes `&` raw inside the block, a few characters after escaping the same value correctly outside it. In the second run the plain-text page receives `<b>&`. Nothing changed between the two runs. Quantified over builds of the unchanged site, each build a separate one-shot `hugo` invocation: | Hugo version | builds | `index.html` published raw `&` inside the block | `index.txt` published `<b>&` inside the block | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | v0.164.0, fresh copy of the site per build | 40 | 25 | 15 | | v0.164.0, fresh copy of the site per build, second run | 40 | 23 | 17 | | v0.165.0, fresh copy of the site per build | 40 | 26 | 14 | | v0.165.0, fresh copy of the site per build, second run | 40 | 28 | 12 | | v0.164.0, repeated builds in one directory | 12 | 8 | 4 | | v0.165.0, repeated builds in one directory | 8 | 5 | 3 | In all 180 of those builds the two output formats carried the *same* string inside the block, so exactly one of the two published files was wrong every time; outside the block the value was escaped correctly for its format in every build. ### What I expected Each format's deferred block rendered under that format's own escaping — `IN[<b>&]` in `public/index.html` and `IN[&]` in `public/index.txt` — and the same result on every build of an unchanged site. The documentation says "The output format, site, and language will be the same, even if the execution is deferred." The output-format *context* does hold up, as the identity-token control below shows; it is the escaping regime that does not follow the output format. ### Controls All of these were run at both v0.164.0 and v0.165.0. **The block really does execute once per output format.** Adding `{{ warnf "DEFER-EXEC-%d" math.Counter }}` to the start of the still byte-identical block body logs two executions in every build: ```text WARN DEFER-EXEC-1 WARN DEFER-EXEC-2 INFO build: step render deferred count 2 duration 1.7497ms --- public/index.html --- OUT[<b>&]IN[&] --- public/index.txt --- OUT[&]IN[&] ``` So this is not one rendering substituted into two files; it is two renderings sharing one escaping mode. **Different `key` values do not separate them.** With `"KH"` in `layouts/home.html` and `"KT"` in `layouts/home.probe.txt`, the block bodies still byte-identical, the escaping stayed shared and kept flipping: 36 builds, 22 with the HTML page wrong and 14 with the plain-text page wrong. **Different block body text does separate them, stably.** Changing the body to `INH[{{ .v }}]` in the HTML template and `INT[{{ .v }}]` in the plain-text template gives the correct per-format result in 36 of 36 builds, with no flip: `INH[<b>&]` in `public/index.html` and `INT[&]` in `public/index.txt`. **The per-format context inside the block is correct.** With the body still byte-identical in both templates, but carrying an output-format identity token next to the value: ```go-html-template {{ $v := "&" }}OUT[{{ $v }}]{{ with (templates.Defer (dict "key" "K" "data" (dict "v" $v))) }}IN[{{ (index page.AlternativeOutputFormats 0).Name }}|{{ .v }}]{{ end }} ``` With exactly two formats configured the single alternative names the *other* one, so `IN[probe|...]` marks the execution that produced the HTML page and `IN[html|...]` the one that produced the plain-text page. That token was correct in 36 of 36 builds, while the escaping of the value beside it in the very same body was shared and flipped across those builds: ```text public/index.html OUT[<b>&]IN[probe|&] public/index.txt OUT[&]IN[html|&] public/index.html OUT[<b>&]IN[probe|<b>&] public/index.txt OUT[&]IN[html|<b>&] ``` ### Where this appears to come from Offered as a lead from reading the source, not as an instrumented finding. `tpl/tplimpl/templatetransform.go`, `handleWith` (v0.164.0, function at line 409) registers the extracted block under a hash of the block body alone, at lines 450-459: ```go inner := withNode.List.CopyList() s := inner.String() ... innerHash := hashing.XxHashFromStringHexEncoded(s) deferredID := tpl.HugoDeferredTemplatePrefix + innerHash ... c.deferNodes[deferredID] = inner ``` Nothing about the owning template, its output format or its media type enters that identifier, so two templates in different output formats with the same body produce the same `deferredID`. `tpl/tplimpl/templatestore.go`, `addDeferredTemplate` (v0.164.0, function at line 916) then keeps only the first registration under that name, and the first owner fixes the parse namespace for whoever comes later: ```go if _, found := t.templatesByPath.Get(name); found { return nil } ... if owner.D.IsPlainText { prototype := t.tns.parseText ... } else { prototype := t.tns.parseHTML ... } ``` That is exactly the escaping regime the two output formats disagree about, and the loser silently inherits the winner's. Which owner gets there first looks order-dependent. `transformTemplates` (function at line 1916) reaches the registrations by ranging `s.templates()` at line 1937, and that iterator's inner loop at line 1784 ranges a `map[nodeKey]*TemplInfo` — the value type of `treeMain`, declared at line 447 — whose iteration order Go randomizes per run. I found no sort on that path. One contrast worth noting: the sibling transform in the same file, `handleWithPartial` (function at line 324), hashes the owning template's name into its identifier at line 335 — `hashing.XxHashFromStringHexEncoded(c.t.Name() + withNodeInnerString)` — while the older defer path does not. I checked the implicated files at v0.164.0, v0.165.0 and master `7b5199fdeff7d7682e9f979f468d55bc7b67b934`: `tpl/tplimpl/templatestore.go`, `tpl/templates/templates.go` and `tpl/template.go` are byte-identical at all three, and `tpl/tplimpl/templatetransform.go` differs at master only outside this path — the `handleWith` lines quoted above are unchanged there, at 405-414. ### A constraint on any fix Hashing the owning template's name into the deferred identifier, the way `handleWithPartial` does, would break something the documentation promises for `key`: "This will, combined with a hash of the template content, be used as a cache key." Two *different layouts of the same output format* with identical bodies and one shared key share a single execution today, and that is worth keeping — at both versions, on a variant of the site above reduced to one output format and with the `page` kind enabled plus one content file, so that `single.html` renders at all, I measured a single `DEFER-EXEC-1` for a `home.html` and a `single.html` written that way, with both pages publishing the shared result. Separating registrations by the property that actually differs here — the owner's `IsPlainText`, or its output format — would fix the escaping while leaving that documented same-format sharing untouched. ### Related, not duplicates - #7774, fixed by #8462 ("Fixes #7774", merged 2021-04-23): per-build nondeterminism in output-format template lookup for shortcodes. Same failure shape, different subsystem, and it predates `templates.Defer`. - #13236: two empty deferred blocks *in the same template* collided on the identifier `__hdeferred/cafc7706cee4572b` and panicked; closed as completed. That is the same body-only identifier, in a different situation — the collision there is inside one template, and the cross-output-format escaping consequence does not come up. I did not find an existing report covering byte-identical `templates.Defer` bodies across output formats. ### What I did not establish - **Which registration wins in any individual build.** I inferred the winner from the escaping in the published output; I did not instrument the running binary to observe the registration. - **Platform generality.** Everything above was measured on one machine, Windows 11, amd64 extended builds. Whether the split differs on another platform or core count is unmeasured. - **Two non-plain-text formats sharing a body.** The escaping observable needs an `isPlainText` format paired with an HTML one, so two HTML-ish formats sharing a body were not tested and the reach across format combinations is unknown.

title: hugo mod npm pack emits a publishable, checkout-named package.json

judge.reasoning: Patch A fixes the issue more completely. It always writes `"private": true` and a fixed, scoped name, `@gohugoio/hugoautogen`. That covers both requests in the issue: the package can't be published, and its name no longer depends on the checkout directory. It also follows the issue's preference for a scoped name, which only the scope owner can claim on the registry. Patch B's default name is the bare `hugoautogen`, which the issue specifically warns anyone can register. Patch B also reads the existing `package.json` and keeps its `name`, `version` and `private` values. Most existing committed manifests were generated by older Hugo and carry the checkout-derived name (e.g. `site-a`). Patch B would keep that bad name indefinitely instead of fixing it. It would likewise keep a stale `private: false`, and it adds a read-parse-merge step with silent fallback on parse errors. Preserving hand-edits is beyond the issue's ask, and here it adds risk by weakening the fix for exactly the repos that reported the problem. Tests: both update the testscript goldens. Patch A's new test seeds a stale checkout-named file and checks that regeneration replaces it with the stable private name. Patch B's test checks the defaults and then that edits are preserved, including `private: false`, which conflicts with the goal of a non-publishable workspace. Patch A also documents the behaviour. A is the better fix.

issue_md:
**TL;DR**: the generated `package.json` has no `"private": true` and a checkout-derived `name`, so committed copies are publishable under names sites don't control. Suggested fix: emit `"private": true` and a stable (ideally scoped) default name.

### What version of Hugo are you using (`hugo version`)?

```
hugo v0.165.0-76a5e1880ab46688155b02e99bab9be2a6134492+extended darwin/arm64 BuildDate=2026-08-12T14:26:28Z VendorInfo=gohugoio
```

### Does this issue reproduce with the latest release?

Yes (transcript below is v0.165.0). The behavior is in master's [package_builder.go](https://github.com/gohugoio/hugo/blob/master/modules/npm/package_builder.go).

### What happened

`hugo mod npm pack` writes `packages/hugoautogen/package.json` with:

- a **name derived from the checkout directory**, so it varies per clone and can be a registry name the site doesn't control, and
- **no `"private": true`**, npm's do-not-publish guard for internal packages.

The file is regenerated wholesale on each run, so hand-set fields don't survive. From a fresh clone of a repo whose committed copy was hand-normalized:

```console
$ git clone https://github.com/google/docsy-example.git site-a && cd site-a
$ grep -E '"(name|version|private)"' packages/hugoautogen/package.json
  "name": "@docsy/hugoautogen",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "private": true
$ hugo mod npm pack
$ grep -E '"(name|version|private)"' packages/hugoautogen/package.json
  "name": "site-a",
  "version": "0.1.0"
```

A sibling clone of the same repo into `site-b` yields `"name": "site-b"`.

### Why it matters

Sites that commit the generated workspace (e.g. so `npm ci` works without running Hugo first) end up carrying a manifest that npm workspace publishing and common release tools treat as publishable by default: `npm publish --dry-run --workspaces` packs it as `site-a@0.1.0`, while with `"private": true` npm skips the workspace. The name variance also churns the committed manifest, and the lockfile's workspace entry, across differently named checkouts.

### What did you expect

The generated internal workspace is non-publishable (`"private": true`) and has a stable, project-controlled default name rather than the checkout directory's basename. Ideally the default is scoped: a bare name can be claimed on the registry by anyone, a scoped one only by the scope owner.

### Workaround

[docsy-example#487](https://github.com/google/docsy-example/pull/487) follows each pack invocation with a single `npm pkg set` line restoring a scoped name and `private`.

Happy to send a PR for the `private` field (and for the name default, if you have a preference for what it should be).
